questions.stem: A 45‑year‑old man presents with a firm, non‑tender mass in the left upper quadrant. Imaging shows a well‑defined, encapsulated lesion arising from the spleen. Which of the following histological findings is most characteristic of a benign splenic cystic lesion?
options: Epithelial lining with cuboidal cells
Fibrous wall with no epithelial lining
Lymphoid aggregates with germinal centers
Malignant epithelial cells with pleomorphism
questions.explanation: Benign splenic cysts are typically true cysts with a fibrous wall and no epithelial lining (pseudocysts). The other options describe epithelial cysts, lymphoid tissue, or malignant changes, which are not characteristic of a benign splenic cyst.
questions.source: Basic surgical pathology of splenic cysts

questions.stem: A 45‑year‑old man presents with a solitary, firm, non‑tender mass in the left upper quadrant. Imaging shows a well‑defined, encapsulated lesion within the spleen. Which of the following histological findings is most characteristic of a benign splenic cyst?
options: Atypical epithelial lining with malignant cells
Fibrous wall with no epithelial lining
Lining of mesothelial cells with clear fluid
Lining of endothelium with thrombosis
questions.explanation: Benign splenic cysts (epithelial cysts) are lined by mesothelial cells and contain clear fluid. A fibrous wall without lining indicates a pseudocyst, while malignant epithelial or endothelial linings would suggest a cystic neoplasm. Thus option C is the best answer.

questions.stem: A 55‑year‑old man presents with a 3‑month history of progressive abdominal distension and early satiety. CT scan shows a large, well‑defined mass arising from the body of the pancreas with cystic degeneration and calcifications. Which histological feature is most characteristic of the tumour type most likely responsible for this presentation?
options: Solid sheets of pleomorphic spindle cells with high mitotic activity
Glandular epithelium forming mucin‑producing ducts
Sheets of uniform cells with a fibrous stroma and psammoma bodies
Well‑differentiated endocrine cells arranged in nests and cords
questions.explanation: The imaging findings are typical of a mucinous cystic neoplasm of the pancreas, which is a cystic epithelial tumour. Histologically it shows mucin‑producing glandular epithelium. The other options describe features of sarcoma, serous cystadenoma (psammoma bodies), and neuroendocrine tumours, which are not consistent with the clinical picture.
questions.source: Pancreatic cystic neoplasms; basic surgical pathology principles

questions.stem: A 58‑year‑old man presents with a 3‑month history of progressive dysphagia to solids, weight loss, and a palpable epigastric mass. Endoscopic biopsy of the mass shows poorly differentiated carcinoma with signet ring cells. Which of the following histopathological features is most characteristic of the underlying tumor type?
options: Presence of mucin‑filled intracytoplasmic vacuoles in a background of desmoplastic stroma
Extensive lymphovascular invasion with perineural spread
High mitotic index with prominent nucleoli in a glandular pattern
Diffuse infiltration by tumor cells forming a solid sheet with little gland formation
questions.explanation: The classic histology of gastric signet‑ring cell carcinoma is mucin‑filled intracytoplasmic vacuoles (signet rings) within a desmoplastic stromal reaction. The other options describe features of different adenocarcinomas or aggressive patterns but are not specific to signet‑ring cells.

questions.stem: A 58‑year‑old man presents with a 4‑cm exophytic mass in the left upper quadrant. Histology shows a spindle‑cell neoplasm with a storiform pattern, high mitotic activity, and areas of necrosis. Immunohistochemistry is positive for S‑100 protein and negative for desmin and cytokeratin. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
options: Leiomyosarcoma
Malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumour
Gastrointestinal stromal tumour
Angiosarcoma
questions.explanation: The spindle‑cell morphology with storiform arrangement and S‑100 positivity is characteristic of a malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumour (MPNST). Leiomyosarcoma would express desmin; GIST is CD117/ DOG1 positive; angiosarcoma shows endothelial markers. The negative desmin and cytokeratin rule out smooth‑muscle and epithelial tumours.
